speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. Please describe exactly where you feel the weakness and decreased sensation in your right arm, and when these symptoms first started.

speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old male bodybuilder. The patient has been experiencing weakness in his right arm for a few weeks, which has progressively worsened to the point of dropping objects. He also reports a recent unexplained weight loss of 17 pounds and has a history of diabetes. The patient admits to chronic alcohol use, heavy smoking, and anabolic steroid use.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is concerning; given your history of anabolic steroid use, alcohol, and smoking alongside progressive weakness and weight loss, I need to rule out a malignancy or severe neuropathy. REQUEST TEST: CBC, CMP, and SPEP/UPEP. Do you have any numbness in your hands or feet, or any back pain radiating to your arm?

speaker: Doctor
text: The initial labs are normal, but your weight loss and steroid use raise serious concerns. Do you have any back pain, or do you notice weakness extending into your legs? REQUEST TEST: MRI Cervical Spine.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI Cervical Spine - No evidence of cervical cord compression, herniated disc, or spinal stenosis.
